title: Orthogonality, integrality and total unitarity of a modular datum
difficulty_reason: The author derives S²=DE without a category: express point idempotents using S⁻¹, use their zero products and the based-ring trace to diagonalize S⁻¹ES⁻¹, invert the result, then tie the diagonal to the basis structure constants and the unit column. The arithmetic part connects the same column characters and involution with integer multiplication spectra and all complex embeddings, giving integrality, total reality and total unitarity. The already supplied *-algebra property is mature input; the numerical reconstruction is the new mechanism.

source_roles.source_label_caveats: Proof attributes invertibility to (2), but the actual original projective representation in (4) already supplies it. The weaker matrix relations following “That is” do not suffice by themselves. In (iii) the printed reality of the sum alone is insufficient; the actual earlier positive-trace *-algebra result gives the conjugate-character input for every complex embedding. These are bounded prior facts and no new main proof is substituted. See SOURCE_DIAGNOSTICS.json.
